questions.q: Why isn't plain RBAC (roles + GRANT) a tight enough ceiling for agent access by itself?
options: An agent inherits every privilege the human's role has, even for the moments where you'd want it to have less
RBAC doesn't apply to agents at all — agents bypass roles entirely
RBAC only works for row-level security, not column-level
Agents can't be assigned roles in Snowflake
questions.explain: An agent runs under a role like anyone else, so it gets every privilege that role grants uniformly — which is often broader than what you'd want an agent specifically to have.

questions.q: In this lesson's masking policy example, what happens when the exact same role (ANALYST) is driven by an agent versus a human?
options: The human sees the real value; the agent sees the masked value, because the policy checks IS_AGENT_ACTIVATED first
Both always see the masked value regardless of who's asking
Both always see the real value regardless of who's asking
The agent sees the real value and the human sees the masked value
questions.explain: The CASE statement checks IS_AGENT_ACTIVATED before checking CURRENT_ROLE(), so an agent gets masked even under a role that would otherwise see the real value.

questions.q: What does Restricted Session Scope (RSS) do?
options: Acts as a privilege ceiling that narrows what an agent can do, without granting anything beyond what the user's own roles already allow
Grants an agent additional privileges beyond the user's roles, for convenience
Replaces RBAC entirely, making roles unnecessary
Automatically masks every column in the account when an agent is detected
questions.explain: RSS is explicitly a ceiling, not a grant — it can only narrow access for agent-active sessions, never expand beyond what the user's roles already permit.

options: By setting AGENT_RESTRICTED_SESSION_SCOPE on a session policy, then attaching that policy to the account or specific users
By adding IS_AGENT_ACTIVATED to every table's primary key
By running ALTER ACCOUNT SET AI_SETTINGS with guardrails enabled
By creating a CLASSIFICATION_PROFILE and attaching it to a database
questions.explain: AGENT_RESTRICTED_SESSION_SCOPE is the session policy setting; the policy is then attached at the account or user level.

questions.q: What is the point of layering RBAC, RSS, masking, and row access policies together for agent access, per this lesson?
options: No single layer has to be perfect — if one is misconfigured, the others still limit the blast radius
Each layer does the exact same job, so layering them is purely redundant and has no practical benefit
Only the last layer configured actually takes effect; earlier ones are overwritten
Layering them removes the need for Agent Identity entirely
questions.explain: Defense in depth means a misconfiguration in one layer (say, a masking policy typo) doesn't expose everything, because RBAC and the other layers still cap what's possible.
